comment: The nine specialist roles give a realistic picture of the skills the architecture requires, and it is helpful that lines 521–524 note that each role does not need a separate post. States with populations under one million face a different problem. Skills such as FHIR modelling, terminology curation, conformance testing and security architecture often do not exist in the national labour market and are seldom sustainable as full-time national posts. The guidance does not yet offer a practical route for these settings beyond building capacity over time.

public.suggestedRevision: Add a short sub-section on shared and regional capacity. It should cover regional pools of specialist skills, jointly procured or operated terminology and conformance services, and regional bodies serving as the institutional home for skills that cannot be sustained nationally. It should also identify which roles remain national, such as architecture ownership, data governance and security accountability, and which can be shared.
